cards.name: Ground acceleration and friction
cards.summary: Ground movement reaches a fixed top speed quickly, then friction pulls the player to a stop.
cards.behavior: NetQuake server code. The intended direction comes from the yaw of the view angles. The server caps the requested speed, measures the shortfall along that direction, and adds acceleration proportional to the requested speed and the frame time, limited by the shortfall. Friction lowers speed each frame by friction times a control speed (never below the stop speed) times the frame time, so slow motion decays gently. When a probe 16 units ahead finds no floor within 34 units below, the friction coefficient doubles, which stops accidental slides off edges.

constants.name: Maximum ground speed
constants.unit: map units/second cap on the requested speed; NetQuake C cvar default sv_maxspeed; a cap with no frame scaling

constants.name: Ground acceleration
constants.unit: per second coefficient; NetQuake C cvar default sv_accelerate; step = coefficient x requested speed x frame time, taken from the server frame time each frame (0.001 to 0.1 s; fixed 0.05 s on a dedicated server)

constants.name: Ground friction
constants.unit: per second coefficient; C cvar default sv_friction; speed lost = coefficient x control speed x frame time, taken from the server frame time each frame (0.001 to 0.1 s; fixed 0.05 s on a dedicated server)

constants.name: Stop speed
constants.unit: map units/second floor for the friction control speed; C cvar default sv_stopspeed; no frame scaling

constants.name: Edge friction multiplier
constants.unit: dimensionless multiplier on friction when a ledge probe finds no floor; C cvar default edgefriction; checked every server frame

cards.name: Air control
cards.summary: Airborne steering has a small speed ceiling, so jumps keep most of their momentum.
cards.behavior: NetQuake server code. When the player is not on the floor, ground friction is skipped and steering uses a separate low cap of 30 units/second on the wished speed when measuring the shortfall. The player can change direction in the air, but each frame adds only a small velocity along the new direction, limited by that shortfall. Existing horizontal momentum stays dominant for the whole jump.

constants.name: Air steering speed cap
constants.unit: map units/second cap on the wished speed used for the air shortfall test; no frame scaling

constants.name: Air acceleration coefficient
constants.unit: per second coefficient (the sv_accelerate default); step = coefficient x full requested speed x frame time, taken from the server frame time each frame (0.001 to 0.1 s; fixed 0.05 s on a dedicated server)

constants.name: Air speed clamp reference
constants.unit: map units/second cap (sv_maxspeed default) on the requested speed; it also scales the air step; no frame scaling

cards.name: Jump impulse
cards.summary: QuakeWorld shared movement code gives a fixed upward velocity only from the ground and only after the jump key is released.
cards.behavior: QuakeWorld movement code (QW/client/pmove.c). The jump input is edge-triggered. A grounded player gets a fixed upward impulse and the jump flag stays set until the key is released, which prevents automatic bunny hopping. In water (waterlevel 2 or more) jump becomes a swim-up speed: 100 in water, 80 in slime, 50 in lava. Facing a low ledge while swimming and not sinking fast starts a separate exit move with an upward push and a forward burst.

constants.name: Jump velocity
constants.unit: map units/second added to vertical velocity once per jump press; instantaneous, not scaled by frame time

constants.name: Water exit upward velocity
constants.unit: map units/second of vertical velocity set once when the ledge exit starts; instantaneous

constants.name: Water exit forward velocity
constants.unit: map units/second of horizontal velocity along the flattened view direction, set once when the ledge exit starts; instantaneous

constants.name: Water swim upward velocity
constants.unit: map units/second of vertical velocity set on each movement command while jump is held in plain water (slime 80, lava 50); not scaled by frame time

cards.name: Water movement
cards.summary: Deep water reduces top speed, adds vertical intent, and makes idle players sink slowly.
cards.behavior: NetQuake server code. At waterlevel 2 (waist) or deeper the mode becomes swimming. Horizontal intent is combined with vertical intent, and zero input gives a slow downward drift. The wished velocity is capped at the ground speed cap, then its speed is multiplied by 0.7. Drag removes a share of all three velocity components each frame, with no stop-speed floor, so direction changes feel heavy and momentum fades quickly.

constants.name: Swimming depth tier
constants.unit: water level number (2 = waist deep) that switches to swim movement; checked every server frame

constants.name: Idle sink rate
constants.unit: map units/second of downward wished velocity when no input is held, before the 0.7 swim factor (so about 42 units/second effective); no frame scaling

constants.name: Swim speed factor
constants.unit: dimensionless multiplier on the wished speed after the sv_maxspeed cap; no frame scaling

constants.name: Water friction
constants.unit: per second coefficient (the sv_friction default, no extra water factor); speed lost = coefficient x speed x frame time, taken from the server frame time each frame (0.001 to 0.1 s; fixed 0.05 s on a dedicated server)

cards.name: Stair stepping
cards.summary: The player climbs low steps by lifting, moving forward, and dropping onto the higher floor.
cards.behavior: NetQuake server code. A normal slide move is attempted first. When it is blocked, the player is lifted by the step height, moved forward at the original horizontal velocity, and dropped by the step height. The landing surface must be flat enough to count as ground. If progress stalls, the server nudges the player in eight directions by a small amount and retries the move.

constants.name: Step height
constants.unit: map units of vertical lift and drop in a walking move; fixed, tried on every blocked walk move

constants.name: Ground normal threshold
constants.unit: dimensionless minimum surface normal Z to count as ground; checked on each landing

constants.name: Unstick probe duration
constants.unit: seconds of simulated time for each unstick retry move; fixed, not tied to the frame time

constants.name: Unstick side step
constants.unit: map units of push per axis for each of the eight retry directions; once per retry

cards.name: Gravity and velocity clamp
cards.summary: Falling speed grows linearly with gravity and is capped per axis before each move.
cards.behavior: NetQuake server code. Every server frame, a walking entity that is not in water adds downward velocity of gravity times its gravity multiplier times the frame time. Each velocity axis is clamped to plus or minus the maximum velocity before integration, so boosts and falls cannot exceed the engine limit. There is no air drag, so fall speed grows at a constant rate until the clamp or a floor stops it.

constants.name: Gravity
constants.unit: map units/second squared; C cvar default sv_gravity; velocity change = gravity x multiplier x frame time, taken from the server frame time each frame (0.001 to 0.1 s; fixed 0.05 s on a dedicated server)

constants.name: Maximum velocity per axis
constants.unit: map units/second per axis; C cvar default sv_maxvelocity; clamped every server frame

constants.name: Default entity gravity multiplier
constants.unit: dimensionless multiplier used when the entity has no gravity field value; applied every server frame

cards.name: Bouncing projectiles
cards.summary: Tossed objects bounce off surfaces with half their normal speed and settle when vertical speed is low.
cards.behavior: Toss-mode entities integrate velocity and gravity, then clip against the first surface. A bounce-type entity removes the surface-normal speed with an overbounce factor of 1.5: a factor of 1 would only slide along the surface and 2 would mirror perfectly, so half of the normal speed returns. On a floor-like surface, low vertical speed or a non-bouncing movetype clears both linear and angular velocity, which brings the object to rest.

constants.name: Bounce reflection multiplier
constants.unit: dimensionless overbounce factor on the surface-normal velocity (1 = slide, 2 = perfect mirror); applied per impact, not frame scaled

constants.name: Settle speed
constants.unit: map units/second of vertical speed after the bounce below which the object stops; checked per floor impact

constants.name: Floor normal threshold
constants.unit: dimensionless minimum surface normal Z for a floor impact; checked per impact

cards.name: View bob
cards.summary: The first-person eye height cycles with horizontal speed and is clamped against extreme offsets.
cards.behavior: First-person view height follows a cycle driven by client time. Amplitude is horizontal speed times the bob scale, blended as 30 percent steady offset plus 70 percent of a sine wave over the cycle. The cycle has a period and a fraction spent rising (0.5 gives equal rise and fall). The final offset is clamped, and standing still removes the effect because speed drives the amplitude.

constants.name: Bob amplitude scale
constants.unit: view height units per map unit/second of horizontal speed, before the 0.3 plus 0.7 sine blend; C cvar default cl_bob; recomputed every rendered frame

constants.name: Bob cycle period
constants.unit: seconds of client time per full cycle; C cvar default cl_bobcycle; not frame scaled

constants.name: Bob upward fraction
constants.unit: fraction of the cycle spent in the rising half; C cvar default cl_bobup; not frame scaled

constants.name: Bob upper clamp
constants.unit: view height units of maximum upward offset; checked every rendered frame

constants.name: Bob lower clamp
constants.unit: view height units of maximum downward offset; checked every rendered frame

cards.name: View roll and damage kick
cards.summary: Side speed rolls the camera, and damage adds a short pitch and roll kick that fades linearly.
cards.behavior: Lateral velocity along the view's right axis rolls the view, scaling linearly up to a small maximum angle. A damage event computes a count (half the blood plus half the armor damage, at least 10), then sets a roll kick and a pitch kick from that count and the direction of the hit. The kick fades linearly to zero over the kick time. Both effects add to the base view angles.

constants.name: Maximum view roll
constants.unit: degrees of roll at or above the full roll speed; C cvar default cl_rollangle; recomputed every rendered frame

constants.name: Full roll speed
constants.unit: map units/second of lateral speed that gives the maximum roll; C cvar default cl_rollspeed; recomputed every rendered frame

constants.name: Kick decay time
constants.unit: seconds of client time over which a kick fades linearly; C cvar default v_kicktime; counted down by the frame time

constants.name: Damage roll kick
constants.unit: degrees of peak roll per unit of damage count, scaled by the sideways component (-1 to 1) of the hit direction; C cvar default v_kickroll; set once per damage event

constants.name: Damage pitch kick
constants.unit: degrees of peak pitch per unit of damage count, scaled by the forward component (-1 to 1) of the hit direction; C cvar default v_kickpitch; set once per damage event

constants.name: Minimum damage count
constants.unit: damage count floor used for the kick size; set once per damage event

cards.name: Mouse look
cards.summary: Mouse counts become view angles through sensitivity and separate yaw and pitch scales.
cards.behavior: Raw mouse counts are scaled by sensitivity, then converted to yaw and pitch by separate degree-per-count values. Pitch is clamped so the view cannot flip past vertical, and roll is clamped separately. Keyboard turning adds a constant angular rate while a key is held, and a speed key raises that rate.

constants.name: Mouse sensitivity
constants.unit: multiplier per mouse count, applied per input sample, rate unverified

constants.name: Yaw per mouse count
constants.unit: degrees per mouse count, applied per input sample, rate unverified

constants.name: Pitch per mouse count
constants.unit: degrees per mouse count, applied per input sample, rate unverified

constants.name: Upper pitch limit
constants.unit: degrees, clamped per client frame, rate unverified

constants.name: Lower pitch limit
constants.unit: degrees, clamped per client frame, rate unverified

cards.name: Third-person camera
cards.summary: A chase view pulls the camera back and up while aiming at the point the player looks at.
cards.behavior: The third-person view starts from the first-person eye point, moves backward along the view direction by the back offset, moves left by the right offset (a positive value moves it left) and sets height to eye height plus the up offset. It then aims at the point the player looks at, found by a trace up to 4096 units. The camera position is not swept against geometry, so walls can block the view. The offsets are user settings.

constants.name: Chase distance
constants.unit: map units behind the eye point along the view direction; C cvar default chase_back; applied every rendered frame

constants.name: Chase height
constants.unit: map units above the eye point in world up; C cvar default chase_up; applied every rendered frame

constants.name: Chase side offset
constants.unit: map units to the player's left (positive value moves the camera left); C cvar default chase_right; applied every rendered frame

cards.name: Shotgun pellets
cards.summary: One shell fires six hitscan pellets inside a small square spread.
cards.behavior: Each pellet traces to the first solid surface within a long fixed range and applies its own small damage. Hits on one target are summed into a single damage event, so a close blast is far stronger than a distant one. The spread is small enough that most pellets hit a nearby target.

constants.name: Pellet count
constants.unit: pellets per shot

constants.name: Damage per pellet
constants.unit: health points per pellet, applied per shot

constants.name: Square spread radius
constants.unit: maximum random offset per axis, as a fraction of the aim direction length, per pellet; applied each shot

constants.name: Pellet range
constants.unit: map units, applied per pellet per shot

cards.name: Super shotgun pellets
cards.summary: The super shotgun spends two shells for fourteen pellets in a wide, flat pattern.
cards.behavior: The super shotgun spends two shells to fire fourteen pellets. Horizontal spread is much wider than vertical spread, so the pattern covers a broad cone at close range and loses effectiveness at distance. A single remaining shell falls back to the normal shotgun.

constants.name: Pellet count
constants.unit: pellets per shot

constants.name: Horizontal spread radius
constants.unit: maximum random sideways offset, as a fraction of the aim direction length, per pellet; applied each shot

constants.name: Vertical spread radius
constants.unit: maximum random vertical offset, as a fraction of the aim direction length, per pellet; applied each shot

cards.name: Rocket ballistics
cards.summary: Rockets fly straight at high speed, deal direct damage, and add a strong blast.
cards.behavior: Rockets travel in a straight line at high speed and expire after a fixed lifetime. A direct hit deals a base amount plus a small random bonus. The blast adds distance-scaled splash damage to other targets, excluding the direct victim.

constants.name: Direct damage
constants.unit: health points per direct hit

constants.name: Direct damage bonus
constants.unit: health points of random direct bonus, applied per hit

constants.name: Splash damage
constants.unit: health points at the blast center, applied per explosion

constants.name: Rocket speed
constants.unit: map units/second of projectile speed, applied per launch

constants.name: Rocket lifetime
constants.unit: seconds of game time, applied per rocket

cards.name: Nailgun ballistics
cards.summary: Nails are fast small projectiles with a short refire delay and two damage tiers.
cards.behavior: Nails are fast, small projectiles with a short refire delay. The normal nail deals light damage. The super nail costs two rounds and deals double damage. Both fly at the same speed and are removed after a few seconds if they hit nothing.

constants.name: Nail damage
constants.unit: health points per nail, applied per hit

constants.name: Super nail damage
constants.unit: health points per super nail, applied per hit

constants.name: Nail speed
constants.unit: map units/second of projectile speed, applied per launch

constants.name: Nail refire delay
constants.unit: seconds between shots, for both nail types, game time

constants.name: Nail lifetime
constants.unit: seconds of game time before an unspent nail is removed; set per nail

cards.name: Lightning beam
cards.summary: The lightning gun traces a short beam that damages targets along its path.
cards.behavior: The lightning gun traces a beam from the player, forward to the first solid surface within its fixed range, and damages targets along it, using two extra side-offset traces to catch neighbors. Each firing step spends one cell. Firing in water deeper than waist level discharges all remaining cells as radial damage instead of a beam.

constants.name: Beam damage
constants.unit: health points per beam hit, applied on each firing step (the animation steps every 0.1 s while the fire key is held)

constants.name: Beam range
constants.unit: map units of reach, applied per shot

constants.name: Underwater discharge damage
constants.unit: health points of radial damage per cell spent; applied once on an underwater shot

cards.name: Grenade ballistics
cards.summary: Grenades arc at moderate speed, bounce, and explode on a fixed fuse.
cards.behavior: Grenades launch at moderate speed with an upward arc and bounce off surfaces. A fixed fuse detonates them, or they detonate on touching a damageable target, and the explosion applies distance-scaled splash damage. Because the fuse runs on game time, a long throw can detonate away from the aim point or after the target has moved.

constants.name: Grenade launch speed
constants.unit: map units/second, applied per throw

constants.name: Grenade upward arc
constants.unit: map units/second of upward velocity, applied per throw

constants.name: Grenade fuse
constants.unit: seconds of game time, applied per grenade

constants.name: Grenade splash damage
constants.unit: health points at the blast center, applied per explosion

cards.name: Damage knockback
cards.summary: Damage pushes walking targets away from the blast and splash falls off with distance.
cards.behavior: Damage to a walking target pushes it along the direction from the blast center at eight speed units per health point. Quad damage multiplies incoming damage before both health loss and push. Splash damage falls off linearly with distance, self-damage is halved, and the search radius exceeds the nominal blast by a margin.

constants.name: Knockback per damage
constants.unit: map units/second of push per health point, applied per damage event

constants.name: Quad damage multiplier
constants.unit: damage multiplier, applied per powered hit

constants.name: Self-damage multiplier
constants.unit: damage multiplier, applied per self-inflicted blast

constants.name: Blast search margin
constants.unit: map units added to blast radius, applied per explosion

constants.name: Splash falloff per distance
constants.unit: health points lost per map unit of distance from the blast center, measured to the target's center; applied per explosion

cards.name: Player collision hull
cards.summary: The player collides as a square box with an asymmetric vertical span.
cards.behavior: The player uses an axis-aligned box for collision, with a square footprint and an asymmetric vertical span. The origin sits inside the box, so the eye point must be offset upward. Movement resolves against this box rather than a capsule, which shapes stair and ledge behavior.

constants.name: Hull minimum X and Y
constants.unit: map units (QuakeWorld shared movement hull, fixed, no time dependence)

constants.name: Hull minimum Z
constants.unit: map units (QuakeWorld shared movement hull, fixed, no time dependence)

constants.name: Hull maximum X and Y
constants.unit: map units (QuakeWorld shared movement hull, fixed, no time dependence)

constants.name: Hull maximum Z
constants.unit: map units (QuakeWorld shared movement hull, fixed, no time dependence)

cards.name: First-person eye height
cards.summary: The first-person camera sits a fixed height above the player origin.
cards.behavior: The default eye point sits a fixed height above the player origin. The view code adds this height before applying bob and pitch. Changing the eye height changes perceived scale without changing the collision box.

constants.name: Default eye height
constants.unit: map units above the player origin; fixed offset added every rendered frame

cards.name: Input speeds and run modifier
cards.summary: Keyboard movement uses fixed speeds, and a speed key doubles them and raises turn rates.
cards.behavior: Keyboard movement builds forward, side, and vertical intent from fixed speeds. Holding the speed key doubles all three intent values. The server then caps the combined speed at the ground speed cap, so a doubled forward speed of 400 or a side speed of 350 is cut to 320. Keyboard turning adds yaw and pitch at fixed angular rates, and the same speed key raises the turn rate.

constants.name: Forward speed
constants.unit: map units/second of intended movement from one key; C cvar default cl_forwardspeed; sampled every input frame, before the server speed cap

constants.name: Side speed
constants.unit: map units/second of intended movement from one key; C cvar default cl_sidespeed; sampled every input frame, before the server speed cap

constants.name: Speed key multiplier
constants.unit: dimensionless multiplier on forward, side and vertical intent; C cvar default cl_movespeedkey; applied every input frame

constants.name: Keyboard yaw rate
constants.unit: degrees/second while a turn key is held; C cvar default cl_yawspeed; multiplied by the client frame time each frame

constants.name: Keyboard pitch rate
constants.unit: degrees/second while a look key is held; C cvar default cl_pitchspeed; multiplied by the client frame time each frame

constants.name: Speed key angle multiplier
constants.unit: dimensionless multiplier on turn rates while the speed key is held; C cvar default cl_anglespeedkey; applied every client frame

cards.name: Swept box collision
cards.summary: Movement sweeps a box through the BSP world and stops at the first blocking surface.
cards.behavior: A move test selects a hull that matches the entity size, sweeps the box from start to end, and returns the first blocking plane, the impacted entity, and the fraction of the path that was clear. Solid entities are linked into the world so nearby triggers and other solids can find them. Moving links also dispatch touch events when a solid overlaps another entity.
